articles.title: The Amputations America Can Prevent
articles.summary: I was born in Nigeria, and raised and educated in New Jersey and New York City. But more than a decade ago, my journey led me to the heart of the Mississippi Delta, a region whose rich history, resilience, hope, and deeply-rooted bloodlines tell a powerful American story. I arrived because I recognized an unmet healthcare need that could no longer be ignored—a disturbing pattern of preventable limb loss that I came to describe as the Black American amputation epidemic . articles.title: The Future of Libraries Is About More Than Books
articles.summary: In considering the role of libraries , I’m often pulled to the words of journalist, author, and longtime editor of Saturday Review , Norman Cousins. “The library is not a shrine for the worship of books,” he wrote in 1954. “It is not a temple where literary incense is burned or one’s devotion to the bound book is expressed in ritual. articles.summary: It can be difficult to sum up a year in a word, but that hasn’t stopped dictionaries from trying. articles.title: The Altruists Rewrites the FTX Collapse as an Implausible Dangerous Liaisons for Nerds
articles.summary: In the four years since FTX collapsed —and the three since the cryptocurrency exchange’s founder, Sam Bankman-Fried , was convicted on multiple fraud charges —its downfall has been squeezed to fit many narrative frames. It’s the Emperor’s New Clothes or Icarus flying too close to the sun. Or maybe it’s a cautionary tale about Bankman-Fried’s guiding philosophy, effective altruism , which encourages adherents to maximize charitable giving by earning a lot of money.
